summary: CBS Sports previews the Day of Reckoning pay-per-view card in Riyadh, headlined by Anthony Joshua vs. Otto Wallin and Deontay Wilder vs. Joseph Parker. Both former heavyweight champions are big favorites, but a win for each could set up a rumored two-fight Joshua-Wilder deal in March 2024 backed by Saudi investment. The article covers backgrounds, quotes, odds, the undercard, and picks of Wilder by KO8 and Joshua by UD12.
one_line: Preview of Saudi Arabia's Day of Reckoning card, with Joshua facing Wallin and Wilder facing Parker as steps toward a Joshua-Wilder fight.
key_facts: Day of Reckoning takes place Dec. 23 at Kingdom Arena in Riyadh, Saudi Arabia, starting 11:30 a.m. ET on DAZN PPV, priced at $39.99.
Anthony Joshua (26-3, 23 KOs) faces Otto Wallin (26-1, 14 KOs) in the main event; Joshua is a -455 favorite and Wallin is +345.
Deontay Wilder (43-2-1, 42 KOs) fights Joseph Parker (33-3, 23 KOs) in the co-main event, returning from a 14-month layoff; Wilder is -650 and Parker +460.
A Joshua vs. Wilder fight is rumored for March 2024 as the first of a two-fight deal, if both win on Saturday.
Eddie Hearn of Matchroom Sport said the card was put together in about six weeks and called Wallin a very dangerous opponent.
Wilder last fought in October 2022, knocking out Robert Helenius in Round 1, after losing the final two fights of his trilogy with Tyson Fury by violent stoppage.
Wilder attended an Ayahuasca retreat in South America and says his mind is in an 'over-happy place'; he earlier fired co-trainer Mark Breland for throwing in the towel in the 2020 Fury rematch.
Joshua lost his titles to Oleksandr Usyk in 2021 and attended a darkness retreat where he spent four days alone in a pitch black room.
Wallin, 33, a southpaw from Sweden, lost a 2019 title shot against Fury but opened a cut requiring 47 stitches above Fury's eye.
Parker, 33, from New Zealand, lost his WBO title to Joshua in 2018, has wins over Andy Ruiz Jr., Hughie Fury and Derek Chisora, and trains under Andy Lee in Tyson Fury's camp.
Undercard includes Dmitry Bivol (-3500) vs. Lyndon Arthur for the WBA light heavyweight title, and Daniel Dubois (-220) vs. Jarrell Miller (+180).
Other undercard bouts: Jai Opetaia vs. Ellis Zorro (cruiserweight), Arslanbek Makhmudov vs. Agit Kabayel, Frank Sanchez vs. Junior Fa, and Filip Hrgovic vs. Mark De Mori.
Author Brian Campbell's picks are Wilder via KO8 and Joshua via UD12.
